tile-installation/longboat-key.title: Tile Installation Longboat Key FL | Porcelain & Stone
tile-installation/longboat-key.description: Tile installation on Longboat Key, floor-to-ceiling porcelain and bookmatched stone for Bay Isles and Longboat Key Club condos, 2026 pricing.
tile-installation/longboat-key.h1: Tile Installation in Longboat Key's Condos and Villas
tile-installation/longboat-key.lede: Floor-to-ceiling porcelain and bookmatched natural stone are the default request on Longboat Key, not the exception, and most of the tile work we quote here is for a primary bath or foyer in a premium renovation.
tile-installation/longboat-key.capsule: Tile installation on Longboat Key runs toward large-format porcelain and natural stone rather than a standard 12-inch square, matching the island's premium condo and villa renovations in Bay Isles and the Longboat Key Club area. Large-format porcelain 24 inches and up runs $9 to $15 per sq ft installed in 2026, natural stone $12 to $22, with curbless shower conversions common in primary baths.
tile-installation/longboat-key.body_html:
Tile installation on Longboat Key skews toward large-format porcelain and bookmatched natural stone more than almost anywhere else in our service area, a direct reflection of the premium condo and villa stock in buildings like L'Ambiance, Grand Bay and the Longboat Key Club. Floor-to-ceiling porcelain in a primary bath and stone in a foyer are close to the default request rather than an upgrade option, and because nearly the entire island sits in an AE or VE flood zone, tile's waterproof nature makes it one of the safest material choices for ground-floor units and lanai-adjacent rooms.

Association sound rules apply to tile the same way they apply to hardwood or vinyl: Florida Building Code sets an IIC/STC floor of 50 between units (45 if field-tested), and a Longboat Key board typically wants the underlayment's lab documentation before approving a hard-surface tile install over a living space below. A 1,600 sq ft mid-rise unit converting from carpet to large-format porcelain throughout would typically need a sound-rated membrane under the tile in every room except the kitchen and baths, adding to both material cost and install time. We walk through that approval process on the condo flooring page before we ever schedule a start date, and our full Longboat Key area guide covers which buildings tend to ask for stone versus porcelain.

Primary-bath work is its own category here. The Water Club and similar buildings see a steady stream of curbless, linear-drain shower conversions with bookmatched stone or large-format porcelain on the walls, a look that reads well in a unit that gets shown to weekend guests. Wet-area safety matters more on an island where sandy, wet feet come straight off the beach, and we default to a textured or matte finish in bath and lanai-adjacent areas rather than the glossy finish some owners initially ask for, a distinction covered in our post on which floor tile isn't slippery when wet. Tile removal ahead of any of this, pulling old glued tile down to the slab, runs through the same crack-isolation check we'd use on the mainland, just with an elevator reservation added to the schedule.
tile-installation/longboat-key.cost_html: A 120 sq ft primary bath in a Longboat Key Club unit, retiled in large-format porcelain at $9-$15 per sq ft installed, runs $1,080-$1,800 in 2026. Converting that same bath to a curbless, linear-drain shower adds $2,800-$5,200, bringing the full bath project to $3,880-$7,000. Natural stone in a foyer or accent wall runs $12-$22 per sq ft, so a 150 sq ft foyer in stone would run $1,800-$3,300 on its own. A standard Kerdi shower pan-and-membrane conversion, without the curbless linear drain, runs $1,800-$3,800. Full category pricing, including stone accent walls and shower packages, lives on our tile installation cost guide.

faqs.q: Is tile a good choice for a ground-floor unit on Longboat Key?
faqs.a: Yes, tile is one of the better ground-floor choices on the island precisely because nearly all of Longboat Key sits in an AE or VE flood zone; a waterproof, hard-surface material like porcelain holds up to a wet-in, wet-out event far better than wood or laminate.

faqs.q: Does my Longboat Key condo association require a sound rating for tile floors?
faqs.a: Yes. Florida Building Code sets an IIC/STC minimum of 50 between units (45 if field-tested), and Longboat Key boards typically want the underlayment's lab report before approving a hard-surface tile install over another owner's ceiling.

faqs.q: What tile finish do you recommend for a Longboat Key primary bath?
faqs.a: A textured or matte porcelain rather than a glossy finish, since sandy, wet feet coming in from the beach make a glossy floor more slippery here than it would be in an inland bathroom.
